chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said:

We were in Makkah, and high prices struck us regarding the sacrificial animals, so we bought it for one Dinar, then for two Dinars, then we could not find it for a small amount nor a large amount. So Hisham al-Mukari wrote a note to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and informed him of what we had bought, then we could not find it for a small amount nor a large amount. So he signed: 'Look at the first price, and the second, and the third, then give in charity the equivalent of a third of it.'
ai.seo_question: How to calculate the value of a sacrificial animal with fluctuating prices according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) addresses the issue of price fluctuation (ghala') during the Hajj season, providing a practical method for valuing sacrificial animals when the exact purchase price is ambiguous. By instructing the companions to consider the first, second, and third prices and donate one-third of the average as charity, the Imam establishes a mechanism to purify the transaction from uncertainty (gharar). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on fairness and the purification of wealth through charitable compensation in cases of financial ambiguity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Umar who said,

‘We were in Makkah, and we were hit by high prices from the sacrificial animal. So we bought it with a Dinaar, then with two Dinars. Then we could not find any, neither for less nor for more. So Hisham Al-Makary wrote a note and sent it to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and informed him<sup>asws</sup> what we had bought, then we could neither find for less nor more’. So he<sup>asws</sup> signed: ‘Consider the first price, and the second, and the third, then give in charity with the likes of a third of it (Average of the three prices)’.
en.sarwar: 22. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar who has said the following:

“Once we were in Makkah and animal for offering became very expensive. We bought for one dinar then, two dinar and then we could not find anything for less or more. Hisham al-Mukariy then wrote a note to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and informed him (the Imam) of what we had bought and then could not find anything for less or more. He (the Imam) then wrote, ‘Consider the first, second and third prices, then give in charity one-third of the average of such prices.’”
